features.headline: Cowboys rave about Quinnen Williams a year after trade deadline deal
features.desc: Voted a captain by his teammates, Williams is making a difference in Dallas on and off the field.
body: FRISCO, Texas — In his past few meetings with the media, Dallas Cowboys defensive tackle Quinnen Williams has come up with a couple of phrases for when he does not want to address a certain subject or does not know enough about one to comment.
One common refrain has been: "I've got to think about that."
Another has been: "I'm going to keep that to myself."
Recently, he said he was not playing in a dominant manner, that he needed to fine tune and fix some things.

"I know exactly how it's supposed to look, how it's supposed to feel when it gets there," Williams said. "Right now, I can just focus on getting better, the things I did wrong, the things I need to do better and keep going in the right direction.
When that game comes, when that game hits, I can build off that with momentum."
Whatever is missing might be the most minute details that only he and limited number of players in his stratosphere can understand.

Williams called his 2022 season with the New York Jets his standard when he had 12 sacks, 12 tackles for loss (TFL), 28 quarterback pressures, four pass breakups, two forced fumbles and a fumble recovery.
Through nine games this season, Williams leads the Cowboys in sacks (five), tackles for loss (14) and forced fumbles (two). He is second in quarterback hurries (29).

"If there's a better interior defensive lineman than him in the league, I haven't been around one in a long time," coach Brian Schottenheimer said. "He's just dominated the way he can change the game."
He has recorded at least two tackles for loss in each of his past four games. Only linebacker DeMarcus Ware (five) has a longer streak by a Cowboy since TFLs began being tracked in 1999.

features.headline: Big plays by Broncos defense in late-game situations keying Denver's 7-2 start
features.desc: The offense has gotten a lot of the credit for the Broncos' late-game heroics, but the defense's knack for big plays is just as important.
body: — Since the start of the 2024 NFL season, no defense has created more sacks than the Denver Broncos (157, 32 more than the next-best team), scored more defensive touchdowns (seven) or been better in the red zone (46.4% touchdown percentage allowed).

But the numbers aren't quite as dominant through nine weeks of the 2026 season, as opponents have moved at a quicker pace and attacked more on first down to keep the Broncos from revving up their pass rush.
Still, the Broncos' defense might have carved out a new category of excellence this season.

During the first half of the 2026 season, this Denver defense has made the plays in the biggest moments, helping the 7-2 Broncos win six one-score games and become the NFL's premier team in crunch time.

"If you look at the sideline [in those moments], everybody knows it's time to make a play," Broncos edge rusher Nik Bonitto said. "... But I feel like we all think we have more work to do and we can be so much better because we don't step back in those times, we want to be there."

Bonitto's strip-sack and fumble recovery at the end of Sunday's win over the Carolina Panthers — the Broncos' fifth straight victory as they enter their bye week — was the latest instance of Denver's defense shutting the door on its opponents.

That work, in concert with quarterback Bo Nix's late-game offensive heroics, have the Broncos in first place in the AFC West and in prime position to be the AFC's No. 1 seed for a second straight season.
Here's a look at some of the big moments that the Broncos' defense has mustered so far in 2026.

features.headline: The Philadelphia Eagles' 2026 trade haul is likely to age well over time
features.desc: Whether Philadelphia wants to go after its QB of the future or build up around Jalen Hurts, it has options.
body: The bright side for the Philadelphia Eagles (2-7) is that once this no-good, snake-bitten, avert-your-eyes season is over with, they'll exit the dust storm with a sack full of valuable NFL draft capital that will make them power players over the next several offseasons.
Eagles general manager Howie Roseman made sure of that.
He pulled off a pair of trades — one back in October and one before the trade deadline — that surpassed expectation and promise to age well over time.
The first was sending center Cam Jurgens and a 2027 seventh-round draft pick to the Baltimore Ravens for a 2028 second-round draft pick and a 2027 fifth-round pick.
Then on Monday, the Eagles traded defensive tackle Jordan Davis to the Jacksonville Jaguars for a 2027 first-round pick and a 2029 second-rounder.

Add in the A.J. Brown deal this offseason that netted New England's first-round pick in 2028 and a fifth-round pick in 2027, and you're talking about a haul that will provide Philadelphia with a wealth of optionality.

They have two first-round picks in both the '27 and '28 drafts, a pair of second-round selections in '28 and '29, and a total of 12 Day 1 or Day 2 selections spanning the next three years with the possibility of adding more via compensatory picks.
It's a good time to be loaded up, as the next couple drafts are projected to be full of talent as some players who have stayed in college longer due to NIL money run out of eligibility.

If the 2026 season ended today, Philadelphia would hold the No. 5 and No. 25 overall selections come April. Whether they want to go after their quarterback of the future or build up the offense around Jalen Hurts, they have the maneuverability they need.

features.headline: Where does Cam Ward stand coming out of the bye?
features.desc: Ward has nine games left to convince the Titans he should be their QB when they open the new stadium in 2027.
body: NASHVILLE, Tenn. — At 1-7, the Tennessee Titans have tried to find a silver lining after almost every game this season. Second-year quarterback Cam Ward's performance in the Titans' 43-36 loss to the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 8 provided the biggest silver lining so far.

Ward surpassed the 300-yard passing plateau (304 yards) and rushed for a career-high 41 yards. The performance serves as evidence that Ward is capable of being an effective quarterback and gives the 2025 No. 1 pick something to build on after the bye week.

Ward appeared relaxed both in the pocket and on the move. He started the game with a precise pass to slot receiver Wan'Dale Robinson on a deep crossing route for a 16-yard gain. The touch on the pass showed a progression from previous missed opportunities this season.

Ward was able to move slightly within the pocket and reset his feet to deliver the accurate throw. Footwork has been a much-discussed area for improvement for Ward all season, and it was on display multiple times against the Bengals.
One of the best examples was a swing pass to Tony Pollard for 8 yards. Pollard was Ward's fifth read on the play.

Not only did he go deep into the progressions of the play, but he also reset his feet to be aligned towards each option as he went through them. Both his feet and eyes worked together, allowing for several accurate throws.
"Last Sunday quarterback-wise, the best tape was Cam Ward," NFL analyst Dan Orlovsky said via Unsportsmanlike on ESPN Radio last Friday. "No.1 just how good he was in the pocket moving with his feet.

features.headline: How Harry Kane rose to win Ballon d'Or and became an England legend
features.desc: Harry Kane went from overlooked youngster to Ballon d'Or winner. Now he's about to become England's record appearance-holder — and possibly their greatest-ever player.
body: Another week, another landmark moment for Harry Kane. Life is like that right now for the England captain, who will become his country's all-time record appearance-maker when leading out the Three Lions against Croatia on Thursday.

It completes a remarkable fortnight for Kane, 33, after he won the men's Ballon d'Or for the first time and signed a new contract with Bayern Munich through to 2029. He is now one of the highest-paid players in Europe, at more than €30 million per year.

Surpassing Peter Shilton's 125-cap England record felt almost impossible for more than three decades, especially for an outfield player. Wayne Rooney reached 120, David Beckham 115, Steven Gerrard 114 and Ashley Cole 107, but Kane will go clear on his own with years still ahead of him.

- Kane's long road to Ballon d'Or glory ends with crowning moment - USMNT or Manchester United: Pros and cons of Pochettino's options - Think less, run more: The rise of man-marking in the Premier League

England's goal-scoring record appeared a similarly difficult climb. Sir Bobby Charlton's tally of 49 stood for 45 years before Rooney reached the half-century in 2015 and later ended on 53. Kane is on a remarkable 91 — and counting.

He has captained England more often than any other player in history, leading England to back-to-back European Championship finals and a third-place finish at this summer's World Cup, the men's national team's best placing since their sole 1966 triumph.

The only thing missing is a major international trophy, something he willingly admits he would trade every individual accolade to have. But Kane's case for becoming England's greatest-ever player grows with each passing season.

features.headline: Patrick and Brittany Mahomes announce baby No. 4 on NFL trade deadline day
features.desc: The couple shared the news on a busy trade deadline day that also brought receiver Josh Downs to Kansas City.
body: Trade deadline day in the NFL brought additions on and off the field for Patrick Mahomes.

The Kansas City Chiefs quarterback and his wife, Brittany, announced Tuesday in a joint Instagram post that they are expecting their fourth child. The couple shared beachside family photos featuring their three children in the announcement.
"Another blessing from God... & then there were 6," they wrote with accompanying emojis.

The announcement means another sibling for daughters Sterling Skye, 5, and Golden Raye, 1, and son Patrick "Bronze" Lavon Mahomes III, 3. Patrick and Brittany were high school sweethearts in Texas before getting married in Hawaii in March 2022.

The family announcement capped a busy day for Mahomes, who also welcomed a new teammate in Kansas City. Earlier Tuesday, the Chiefs acquired wide receiver Josh Downs and a 2027 seventh-round pick from the Indianapolis Colts for fourth- and fifth-round selections.
